Date of Release:  October 9, 1992                         No.
22864

Victoria
Registry

IN THE SUPREME COURT OF
BRITISH COLUMBIA

BETWEEN:                         )

)

JANET JOSEPHINE COHEN            )

)
REASONS FOR JUDGMENT

PETITIONER        )

)
OF THE HONOURABLE

AND:                             )

)
MR. JUSTICE DRAKE

AMNON MICHEL COHEN               )

)

RESPONDENT        )

W. M. Hitch
Counsel for the Petitioner

G. Botting
Counsel for the Respondent

Date and Place of Hearing
September 25 and 28, 1992

Victoria, B.C.

The issues in this case are
the custody of the children of the parties, their maintenance, and the division
of the matrimonial property.  Counsel have furnished me with helpful trial
briefs.

Mr. and Mrs. Cohen were
married in September 1978.  There are three sons of the marriage, Opheer Olam
born 13 June 1979, Yarom Olam born 26 October 1981, and Aviaud Olam born 17 May
1988.  The parties separated finally on 2 September 1989, following assaults on
Opheer and Mrs. Cohen by Mr. Cohen:  charges were laid, and Mr. Cohen, on 8
December 1989, was convicted of two assaults, receiving a total sentence of
eighteen months probation with specific conditions which included a prohibition
against him having

- 2 -

any contact with his family without
the approval of his probation officer.  This prohibition would have continued
until 8 June 1991.  On 6 June 1990, Mrs. Cohen commenced divorce proceedings.
Various interim orders were made by this Court as follows:

27 June 1990
:
Master Patterson ordered that Mrs. Cohen have
custody of the three children, exclusive possession of the matrimonial home,
and ordered as well the preparation of a custody and access report -- which was
done, and I have seen it.

31 July 1990
:
Master Halbert ordered that Mr. Cohen would
have access to the children, the terms of which he specified in detail, and
further, enjoined Mr. Cohen from harassing Mrs. Cohen or attending at her
residence except for picking up and returning the children in the course of
access visits.  Mr. Cohen has on more than one occasion been in breach of this
order.

30 April 1991
:
There was a "desk" order granting a
decree nisi of divorce to Mrs. Cohen, giving her sole custody of the children,
providing for maintenance for them, and vesting Mr. Cohen's interest in the
matrimonial home in Mrs. Cohen.

26 September 1991
:
Murphy, J. set aside the provisions of this
order, save for the decree nisi, revived the orders of the two Masters, and
left the question of the ownership of the matrimonial property to be determined
by the Court in due course.

- 3 -

Before me now is the matter
of the final determination of the issues I have set out above.

Mr. Cohen is a marine
engineer, having qualified as such in a prestigious institution in Israel,
described as the equivalent as the United States Naval Academy at Annapolis,
Maryland.  Mrs. Cohen is a registered nurse in British Columbia who stands
high in her profession and specializes in paediatrics.  She has been,
throughout the marriage, the effective breadwinner of the family:  and has worked
prodigiously to upgrade her qualifications and rear her three children at the
same time.  Mr. Cohen has spent the most of his time since 1978 working on
inventions, none of which so far have produced anything remunerative.  For most
of this time, Mr. Cohen has lived on social assistance.  The evidence regarding
the prospects of his inventions is not such as to persuade me that much can be
hoped for in the future.  While Mrs. Cohen was working, he functioned as a
house-husband; but I am unable to find that his contribution to the family in
this regard has been any more than minimal:  the greater burden of housekeeping
and child rearing fell throughout on his wife.

Mr. and Mrs. Cohen own, in
joint tenancy, a house currently appraised at $185,000.00, encumbered by a
mortgage and tax arrears to the extent of about $110,000.00 (round figures),
leaving a net equity of some $75,000.00.  Mr. Cohen's contribution to the
purchase and upkeep of this house were insignificant.

- 4 -

It would be fruitless to go
into the sad state of this marriage at length.  Suffice it to say that after a
romantic start involving much world travel, the relationship gradually
deteriorated to the point that, when the parties separated in September of
1989, they had found it convenient to establish a mutual bond of inveterate
hatred: and rational communication between them is no longer possible.

My concern here is with the
best interests of the three boys, and with such provision as can be made for
their maintenance.  Mrs. Cohen seeks final confirmation of her order for
interim custody, and Mr. Cohen asks for an order for joint custody.  In view of
my findings as to the compatibility of the parents, joint custody is simply not
practical:  and would make life even more difficult for the children than it is
now.  So Mrs. Cohen will have custody of the children as heretofore, and she
will be their sole guardian.

I have been much troubled by
the matter of access.  There are reasons to believe that Mr. Cohen's influence,
not only on them, but on his wife, has been a disrupting factor in their
lives.  For example, his preference is to limit his visits to one boy at a
time:  and there is also the fact that he has mistreated Opheer in the past,
and may well be mistreating him in one way or another at present.  Opheer is
thirteen, the age at which he ought to be prepared for his bar mitzvah; and his
father has taken no steps at all to prepare him.  Opheer, at present, is a
confused and troubled        - 5 -

boy, and is undergoing treatment at
Jack Ledger House, a psychiatric institution for children and adolescents.  The
main reason for this is the hostility between his parents:  in my belief, the
ultimate responsibility for this sad situation lies with his father.

The two younger boys seem to
be doing reasonably well at present under the interim access arrangements now
in force -- that is, one day of each weekend as set out in Master Halbert's
order of 30 July 1990.

On the other hand, children,
especially boys in a Jewish family -- even in one where, I am persuaded,
religion plays no large part -- ought to know and be known by their father.
Access for all, then, should continue on the same terms as previously ordered:
and even though liberty to apply is always implicit in such orders, I think it
well to mention clearly that there will be liberty to apply here.  Situations
change as children grow.  I also emphasize the provision of the Master's order
as to leaving Mrs. Cohen alone and keeping out of the matrimonial
residence; which injunction remains in full force until further order.

As to maintenance for the
boys -- Mrs. Cohen is not seeking it for herself -- Mr. Hitch suggests this
should be in lump sum form.  I agree.  The only steady job Mr. Cohen has held
for many years is a low paying one, driving a truck for the St. Vincent de Paul
Society.  He has only held this during the past summer, and  - 6 -

it is not really a career.  The
possibility of him being in a position to make reasonable periodic payments is
not realistic.  Mr. Hitch also suggests that the lump sum payments for each boy
be secured by their father's equity in the matrimonial home.  Since this will
be the only fund -- or potential fund -- which could provide for their
maintenance in the way of lump sum, and since their mother's income from her
profession is adequate for their day to day needs, such a disposition is
appropriate.

Mr. Cohen's undivided half-interest
in the matrimonial home should be conveyed to Mrs. Cohen in trust for the three
boys.  It is unnecessary, in these circumstance, to make any division of this
property under the
Family Relations Act
:  but it is to be noted
that Mr. Cohen's contribution to its acquisition has been so insignificant as
to be negligible in any event.

Concerning what few chattels
remain, I make the same order as did Master Halbert:  but Mr. Cohen should
return the Star of David and Mesuza which he removed from the residence.

There will be no order as to
costs.

"M.L.T. Drake, J."

October 7, 1992

Victoria, B.C.
